identitySignals: Name matches exactly: Alpine Academy, a Utah residential treatment school (alpineacademy.org), certified as a non-public school, matching OUSD's 'Nonpublic, Nonsectarian School/Agency' special education master contracts
Located in Utah, matching the agenda's Salt Lake City, UT; its operator Utah Youth Village is headquartered in Salt Lake City, UT
Alpine Academy's own site states it was created in 2001 as a program of Utah Youth Village, a nonprofit, and Utah Youth Village's site lists Alpine Academy as one of its programs
Academics are taught by dual-endorsed special education teachers for students with emotional disturbances, consistent with the special education contract purpose
research.notes: Alpine Academy is a program of Utah Youth Village; the registered legal entity and EIN are Utah Youth Village's (ProPublica lists it in Holladay, UT; its site gives 5800 South Highland Drive, Salt Lake City, UT 84121, phone (801) 272-9980). Phone and address shown are Alpine Academy's own (Mountain View Campus, Erda; a second campus is at 1492 Meadowbrook Dr., Tooele, UT 84074). No general email found. California and SAM.gov registry entries were not checked.

profile.summary: Alpine Academy is a residential treatment school for teens ages 12 to 18 in Utah. It has separate campuses for males and females and combines therapy, residential care and classroom academics. It is a program of Utah Youth Village, a nonprofit founded in 1969.

sources.title: Utah Youth Village - Nonprofit Explorer - ProPublica

review.notes: Alpine Academy (Utah, Salt Lake area, special-education nonpublic school) is stated on its own site as a program of Utah Youth Village (nonprofit, founded 1969), and ProPublica confirms the EIN and legal name; phone, address, ages and campuses are supported. The headquarters value 'Erda, UT' is the campus location, not the legal entity's headquarters (Utah Youth Village is in Salt Lake City/Holladay), so it is dropped.
